ukmt-pink-2022-07.title: Pythagoras with areas
ukmt-pink-2022-07.body:
The central square is built on the hypotenuse of both right-angled triangles. By Pythagoras, the square on the hypotenuse has area equal to the sum of the areas of the squares on the other two sides.

Left triangle: central square $=22+3=25$. Right triangle: $25=7+{?}$, so the unknown area is $25-7=18$.

**Answer: (A) 18**

ukmt-pink-2022-11.title: Find all possible ages
ukmt-pink-2022-11.body:
Try the ages near the guesses. If Gran is 77, the errors are $2$ (for 75), $1$ (for 78) and $4$ (for 81): this works. If Gran is 79, the errors are $4$ (for 75), $1$ (for 78) and $2$ (for 81): this also works.

Both $77$ and $79$ fit the information, so Gran's age cannot be determined.

**Answer: (E) impossible to determine**

ukmt-pink-2022-20.title: Look at the corners
ukmt-pink-2022-20.body:
At each corner of the cube three squares meet, one from each of three faces, and each pair of them shares an edge. So the three squares at a corner must show three different shapes: one cross, one triangle, one circle.

Each of the 24 squares touches exactly one corner, and the cube has 8 corners, so there are exactly $8$ crosses, $8$ triangles and $8$ circles. None of the options (A) to (D) has this, so none is possible.

**Answer: (E) none of these are possible**

ukmt-pink-2022-22.title: Find a right angle
ukmt-pink-2022-22.body:
Let $S$ be the point on the line where the two squares touch, $R$ the top-left corner of the larger square and $Q$ the top-right corner of the smaller square. The diagonal $RS$ of the larger square goes up and to the left from $S$ at $45^\circ$ to the line, and the diagonal $SQ$ of the smaller square goes up and to the right from $S$ at $45^\circ$ to the line. So $\angle RSQ=45^\circ+45^\circ=90^\circ$.

Triangle $RSQ$ is right-angled with legs $RS=10$ and $SQ=8$, so its area is $\frac12\cdot10\cdot8=40$ cm$^2$.

$P$ is the centre of the smaller square, so it is the midpoint of the diagonal $SQ$. Triangles $PQR$ and $RSQ$ have the same height from $R$ and bases $PQ=\frac12 SQ$, so the area of $PQR$ is $\frac12\cdot40=20$ cm$^2$.

**Answer: (B) 20**
